name: Visual Basic
note: Event-driven BASIC dialect that brought rapid GUI development to Windows
typeSystem: Originally weakly/dynamically flavoured via the Variant type, though explicit Dim statements could declare static types; classic VB6 sits between old-school BASIC's dynamic style and .NET's fully static type system introduced later in VB.NET.
runtime: Classic Visual Basic used p-code in early releases, while VB5 and VB6 could produce either interpreted p-code or native x86; both modes depended on a shared VB runtime DLL. VB.NET compiles to CIL for the .NET runtime.

runtimes.name: Native + VB runtime DLL (VB5/6)
runtimes.role: VB5 and VB6 can compile to native x86 while still depending on a shared runtime library for startup, forms, controls, and core functions.

runtimes.name: P-code + VB runtime
runtimes.role: Classic releases use or optionally emit compact p-code interpreted by the Visual Basic runtime; VB5 and VB6 offer both p-code and native output.

runtimes.name: .NET CLR (VB.NET)
runtimes.role: Modern Visual Basic .NET compiles to CIL bytecode, JIT-compiled by the CLR, sharing its runtime with C#.

compilers.name: VB6 compiler
compilers.role: Microsoft's classic Visual Basic 6 compiler, targeting either p-code or native Windows applications.

concurrencyModel: Ordinary classic VB applications are predominantly event-loop based, but VB6 ActiveX components support COM apartment threading, including thread-per-object or configured pools for out-of-process servers. VB.NET uses the full .NET threading and Task-based async/await model.

codeExample.caption: Hello, World!
codeExample.source:
Module Program
    Sub Main()
        Console.WriteLine("Hello, World!")
    End Sub
End Module
